summary: Trace hook proxy strips tracing headers leading to orphaned trace links in dashboard panels
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using the console's trace-to-dashboard links intermittently see 'Trace not found' when opening spans from dashboard panels. The problem is concentrated for requests routed through our new edge proxy in front of the api-gateway.

Impact:
- NimbusAI reports 12% of dashboard trace-links failing for recent spikes, causing loss of triage context for SLO alerts.
- Affects live incident troubleshooting and alert jump-to-trace workflows in Console.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) behind edge-proxy v1.4.2 -> api-gateway v3.0.5 -> tracing-ingest cluster.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From Console, open a dashboard panel with a trace-linked timeseries (example org project + route).
2) Click an alert/trace link for a failed request within the panel.
3) In ~10-30% of tries, Console opens the trace page with 'Trace not found' even though the span exists in tracing ingest.

Observed logs / artifacts:
- Console link contains trace_id and span_id query params.
- Tracing ingest shows the span (verified by trace_id) but the Console backend receives a Trace-Context header with trace_id missing or truncated for failing cases.
- Edge-proxy access logs show the same request IDs for success and failure; difference is presence of 'traceparent' and 'tracestate' headers in upstream payloads.
- Reproduced by enabling debug capture on proxy: failing requests have trace headers removed when route uses header-normalization rule 'strip-internal'.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: header normalization rule on edge-proxy strips the W3C trace headers for requests routed from some client IP ranges.
What we did:
- Captured pcap and request samples for successful and failed link clicks.
- Verified that Console builds trace lookup requests using headers sent from browser -> proxy -> api-gateway. For failing cases, api-gateway receives no traceparent.
- Confirmed tracing ingest still has the span because the original service injected trace headers when calling the model serving runtime; headers present in service-to-ingest path.
- Reproduced locally by toggling 'strip-internal' header-normalization rule in proxy; when enabled, traceparent is removed for requests marked as 'health-check' or with missing user-agent; our dashboard link clicks sometimes matched that predicate when an A/B experiment inserted a synthetic UA.
Policy risk: header normalization was intended to remove vendor-internal headers but a mis-scoped predicate matched legitimate client requests.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Aisha Thompson): Customer reported spikes in 'Trace not found' for dashboard trace-links. Provided early capture and asked for production poke.
2026-03-10 11:48 - SRE (Miguel Hernandez): Reproduced locally with proxy rule. Created staging test to toggle header-normalization. Linked INT-4021 to track proxy rule change request.

2026-03-11 15:03 - Support (Sofia Patel): Notified NimbusAI of partial mitigation: we can temporarily disable header-normalization for the affected edge pool. They requested timeline and risk assessment.
2026-03-12 08:27 - SRE (Miguel Hernandez): Patch PR opened to narrow predicate and add explicit allowlist for traceparent/tracestate: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/912
resolution_notes:
Temporary mitigation: turned off 'strip-internal' normalization for us-east edge pool at 2026-03-11 18:20 UTC — immediate reduction in failures to <1%.
Permanent fix: PR 912 adjusts predicate logic and adds automated integration test to assert W3C trace headers are never removed for requests containing trace_id query params. Plan: roll to prod after canary on 2026-03-14.
Follow-ups: add dashboard-level healthcheck to surface trace-link missing-rate and create runbook step to check proxy header rules (assigned to networking team).
next_steps:
- Complete PR review and canary deploy (SRE)
- Add console metric alert for trace-link failure ratio > 2% (Observability)
- Document header-normalization rules and exceptions on Confluence (Networking + Support)
